title: China accuses the US of ‘AI hegemonism’ and threatens countermeasures
excerpt: China’s commerce ministry accused the United States of “AI hegemonism” on Monday and warned that it would retaliate, an escalation in a quarrel that started with an accusation of copying and has since pulled in chips, sanctions, and a pair of senior White House officials. The ministry said Washington was threatening Chinese companies with punishment on the […]
content_html:
China’s commerce ministry accused the United States of “AI hegemonism” on Monday and warned that it would retaliate, an escalation in a quarrel that started with an accusation of copying and has since pulled in chips, sanctions, and a pair of senior White House officials.

The ministry said Washington was threatening Chinese companies with punishment on the basis of allegations alone, and it cast the whole affair as an effort to hold back China’s technology sector rather than a genuine grievance about intellectual property.

The trigger was distillation, the practice of training a weaker model on the outputs of a stronger one.

White House Office of Science and Technology Policy director Michael Kratsios alleged that the Beijing firm Moonshot AI had distilled Anthropic’s Claude to build its Kimi K3 system, and that it had done so at industrial scale through a purpose-built internal platform designed to dodge detection.

The White House had already put China on notice over the practice, though enforcing any of it remains the hard part.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went further, warning that firms caught running covert distillation attacks could face financial sanctions or a place on the Commerce Department’s Entity List, which would cut them off from American chips and software. That sanction threat is what appears to have prompted Beijing’s response.

The ministry’s language was measured but firm. “For any action that causes substantive harm to Chinese interests, China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests,” an unnamed spokesperson said, without spelling out what those measures might be.

The ministry also rejected the underlying charge, arguing that distillation is a widely used technique, and that the US had produced neither factual nor legal grounds for the punishment it was threatening.

The complaint that started all this came from Anthropic itself. Earlier this year the company told US lawmakers that three Chinese firms, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax, had generated more than 16 million interactions with Claude using roughly 24,000 fraudulent accounts, extracting capabilities in reasoning, coding, and computer vision that they then folded into their own systems.

It later named Alibaba’s Qwen lab as the source of an even larger distillation campaign, and it has used the findings to argue for tighter chip export controls, on the logic that restricting access to advanced semiconductors constrains both direct training and the distillation that feeds off it.

Moonshot has denied the charge. The company said the gains in Kimi K3 came from its own architectural work rather than from copying a rival, a line that echoes the broader Chinese position that Washington is dressing up commercial protectionism as a security concern.

Whether US regulators accept that is a separate question, and one the Entity List does not require them to answer before acting.

The chip dimension runs underneath all of it. Washington has spent the past year closing loopholes that let Nvidia’s most advanced processors reach Chinese buyers through overseas subsidiaries, and reporting tied to the Moonshot case describes the company sourcing Nvidia GB300 chips and routing work through servers in Thailand.

Neither Beijing nor Washington has confirmed those specifics on the record, and Anthropic’s own tally of the traffic it attributes to Moonshot has not been independently audited.

Notably absent from Monday’s exchange was any mention of a Section 301 trade investigation, the tariff mechanism the US has reached for against foreign technology rules elsewhere. This fight is narrower, and for now it is aimed squarely at a handful of Chinese AI labs and the models they have shipped.

What comes next is procedural. Bessent’s warning describes a possible sanction, not one that has been imposed, and no company has yet been added to the Entity List over distillation. The ministry’s countermeasures remain unspecified. For the moment both sides have staked out positions and left themselves room, which is its own kind of signal.

content_html_zh:
中国商务部周一指责美国实行“人工智能霸权主义”，并警告称将进行报复。这场争吵从指控抄袭开始，随后又涉及筹码、制裁和两名白宫高级官员。

该部表示，华盛顿仅仅因为指控就威胁对中国企业进行惩罚，并将整个事件视为遏制中国科技行业的努力，而不是对知识产权的真正不满。

触发因素是蒸馏，即根据较强模型的输出来训练较弱模型的做法。

白宫科技政策办公室主任 Michael Kratsios 声称，北京公司 Moonshot AI 已经从 Anthropic 的 Claude 中提炼出来，构建了 Kimi K3 系统，并且通过一个旨在躲避检测的专用内部平台，在工业规模上做到了这一点。

白宫已经就这种做法向中国发出了警告，尽管执行任何措施仍然是困难的部分。

财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）更进一步警告说，被发现进行秘密蒸馏攻击的公司可能会面临财务制裁或被列入商务部实体名单，这将切断它们与美国芯片和软件的联系。 这种制裁威胁似乎促使北京做出反应。

该部的语言谨慎但坚定。 一位不愿透露姓名的发言人表示：“对于任何对中国利益造成实质性损害的行为，中方将采取一切必要措施，坚决维护自身合法权益。”但他没有具体说明可能采取哪些措施。

该部还驳回了这一基本指控，认为蒸馏是一种广泛使用的技术，美国没有为其威胁的惩罚提供事实或法律依据。

引发这一切的抱怨来自 Anthropic 本身。 今年早些时候，该公司告诉美国立法者，DeepSeek、Moonshot 和 MiniMax 三个中国公司使用大约 24,000 个欺诈账户与 Claude 进行了超过 1600 万次互动，提取了推理、编码和计算机视觉方面的能力，然后将这些能力融入到自己的系统中。

后来，它把阿里巴巴的 Qwen 实验室命名为更大规模的蒸馏活动的源头，并利用这些发现来主张加强芯片出口管制，其逻辑是限制先进半导体的获取，既限制了直接培训，也限制了由此产生的蒸馏。

Moonshot 否认了这一指控。 该公司表示，Kimi K3 的收益来自于自己的建筑作品，而不是抄袭竞争对手，这一说法呼应了中国更广泛的立场，即华盛顿正在将商业保护主义包装成安全问题。

美国监管机构是否接受这一点是一个单独的问题，实体清单并不要求他们在采取行动之前回答这一问题。

芯片尺寸在其下方。 华盛顿在过去的一年里一直在堵住让英伟达最先进的处理器通过海外子公司到达中国买家手中的漏洞，与登月案相关的报道描述了该公司采购英伟达 GB300 芯片并通过泰国的服务器路由工作。

北京和华盛顿都没有证实这些细节，Anthropic 自己对 Moonshot 流量的统计也没有经过独立审计。

值得注意的是，周一的交流中没有提及 301 条款贸易调查，这是美国针对其他地方的外国技术规则所采取的关税机制。 这场战斗的范围较小，目前它的目标是少数中国人工智能实验室及其已交付的模型。

接下来的事情是程序性的。 贝森特的警告描述了一种可能的制裁，但尚未实施，而且尚未有公司因蒸馏而被添加到实体名单中。 该部的对策尚未具体说明。 目前双方都已表明立场并给自己留有余地，这本身就是一种信号。
